name: mergestorm-mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Current Mergestorm API key prefix, plan, API base, and the version of this running mergestorm-mcp server.

tools.name: credits
tools.description: Current standard-credit usage and reset time.

tools.name: review_list
tools.description: List recent Mergestorm review jobs as job envelopes.

tools.name: review_submit
tools.description: Submit a local git diff (or an explicit diff) as a Mergestorm review job. Does not wait by default; returns job_id immediately after submission. Explicit wait: true polls one 45s slice by default. Record job_id and loop review_wait until done. Do not pass 300; hosts drop long MCP calls. On rate_limited, wait retry_after_seconds and inspect or wait for an in-flight review before resubmitting. specialists may be security, performance, architecture, tests, data, api, frontend. governance and seam cannot be requested.

tools.name: review_wait
tools.description: Read one local Mergestorm review job by the job_id that review_submit returned, as a job envelope. timeout_s: 0 reads it once without polling; otherwise it polls for one 45s slice by default (max 300s). On timeout, returns in_progress; call again with the same job_id until done. Do not pass 300; hosts drop long MCP calls. On rate_limited, wait retry_after_seconds before trying again.

tools.name: review_wait_pr
tools.description: Read the Vortex pass on a GitHub PR from the DB-only endpoint; review identity is head SHA + pass. timeout_s: 0 reads it once without polling; otherwise it polls for one 45s slice by default (max 300) and returns in_progress on timeout so you can call again, or none when no review exists for that PR and head yet (call once more; if it is none again, Vortex is not reviewing that head: comment @mergestorm-vortex review on the PR, run mg review, or push a new commit). Pass after_sha for the head you pushed and pass to read one exact attempt; when you already hold a resting envelope for that head, also pass after_pass set to its pass and keep it unchanged across retries; never replace it with the pass of an in-progress envelope, and omit after_pass for a head you hold no envelope for. With timeout_s: 0, a pass that does not exist yet returns not_found, so after a push use a positive timeout. Do not pass 300; hosts drop long MCP calls. On rate_limited, wait retry_after_seconds before trying again. After a resting pass, verify each finding; prefer the smallest correct patch; if you skip, post a PR comment starting with mergestorm-loop: dismiss.

tools.name: review_dismiss
tools.description: Record an audited dismissal of Vortex findings you verified are wrong or not actionable on a GitHub PR. Identity is exact: head_sha must be the PR's live head, review_id a Vortex review (Core or seam) made at that head, and finding_ids the GitHub review comment ids of that review (offdiff-<n> for a body-only finding), or scope "review" with no finding_ids to dismiss every finding of that review. reason must say why (at least 20 characters); evidence_url is optional. Call with preview: true first to list the review's finding ids and the seam gate without writing. The caller's linked GitHub account needs write access to the repository. A moved head, another review, an unknown id or a missing permission is refused and nothing is written. Retries are idempotent. The seam gate clears only when every finding of that integration review is dismissed; the Vortex gate at the head clears only once every Vortex Blocker (error finding) at that head is dismissed and no Vortex review of it is running (gate.vortex.cleared, else gate.vortex.message); CI and Auto land policy are unchanged. Vortex does not raise a dismissed finding again on the same diff. Never dismiss a finding you did not check. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: issue_create
tools.description: Open a GitHub issue through Mergestorm with no GitHub credentials: the Surge App creates it and names you in the body. Use it for the issue a pull request must have before it is opened, then put Fixes #<number> in the commit or pull request body. Defaults to the origin repository of cwd; pass owner and repo together to name another. labels must already exist on the repository; an unknown one is refused with unknown_label and nothing is created. Calling it again with the same title returns the open issue it already made (created: false) when that issue is among the newest 100 open issues of the repository; an older one, or two calls at the same time, can still create a duplicate, so check the returned number before retrying after a lost response. Needs write access to the repository through your linked GitHub account and Surge installed on it.

tools.name: stack_adopt
tools.description: Adopt an open GitHub PR chain into a Mergestorm stack. auto_land is boolean; auto_review, auto_patch, auto_resolve_conflicts, and auto_fix_ci accept true, false, or null, where null clears the override. Omitted auto_land seeds from auto_land_default; omitted overrides are not seeded. Never changes account settings. Adoption needs the Mergestorm Surge GitHub App on the repository. Stacks, the merge queue and Auto land run through that App; Cyclone is the auto-patch App. Without it the API returns cyclone_not_connected or cyclone_not_installed; the message, and error.reason starting with surge_ when Surge is the one to install, say which App is missing — do not retry, tell the human what the message says. Read stack_status with result.stack.id afterward to verify policy and Cyclone ownership. With 2+ PRs, adopt moves the bottom PR's GitHub base to mg-stack-<n> and parks PR3+ on an mg-park-* freeze; a 1-PR stack stays on main. Leave those bases. Never retarget the bottom back to main. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: stack_list
tools.description: List the current user's Mergestorm stacks.

tools.name: stack_publish
tools.description: Publish a local branch without any GitHub credentials. Reads the branch's commits from the local repository at cwd (never runs gh, git push or git fetch) and sends them to Mergestorm, which writes the exact commits and the branch on GitHub as the Surge App, opens a ready pull request when the branch has none, and registers the stack with Auto patch pinned off, Auto land on for a new stack, and Auto review left to the account. These are your own changes; Cyclone does not write or patch them. Use it for the first publication and for every later commit to that branch. Defaults: owner and repo from origin, the checked-out branch, the repository's trunk as base, title and body from the tip commit. Mergestorm verifies each commit's Git tree before it moves the branch and returns the verified head and tree. It refuses with head_changed when the branch on GitHub holds work your local branch does not, base_changed when the base commit left the base branch, protected_branch for trunk and Mergestorm-owned branches, and payload_too_large beyond 20 commits, 500 changed paths, 2 MiB a file or 8 MiB in total; submodules and merge commits are not carried. replace_head replaces that exact GitHub head with the local branch and discards its commits. Safe to call again after a lost response or a failure: it resumes and never duplicates the branch, commits, pull request or stack. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: stack_publish_status
tools.description: Read how far a branch published with stack_publish got: absent, pushed (branch on GitHub, no pull request), opened (pull request open, stack not registered) or registered, with the head commit and tree on GitHub, the pull request and the stack's Auto patch and Auto land state. Changes nothing. Call it after a lost stack_publish response, then call stack_publish again to resume.

tools.name: stack_set
tools.description: Set per-stack automation on one owned Mergestorm stack: auto_land arms or disarms Auto land; auto_review, auto_patch, auto_resolve_conflicts, and auto_fix_ci pin Vortex auto-review, Cyclone auto-patch, Auto-resolve merge conflicts, or Auto-fix failing CI for this stack only (true or false), and null clears the pin so the stack follows the account setting again. Pass at least one key. Never changes account settings. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: stack_status
tools.description: Fetch one owned Mergestorm stack with enriched checks and agent state, plus attention, issues, and currentCandidate from the same blocker rules as stack_wait, read against that stack's own merge queue. trunkBranch is mg-stack-<n> for an adopted 2+ PR stack and matches the bottom open PR's GitHub base; an mg-park-* parentBranch is a freeze. Neither is drift to fix. repair names the concrete fix for attention; landGatePending is a wait, not attention. held names a blocker no agent run clears while Vortex or Cyclone is still busy on that PR (actAfter agents_idle, waitingOn); repair then describes the fix to plan, not to apply yet. Auto land off after a merge_failed, gh_error, or ci_timeout bounce (the stack's autoLandOff reads reason bounced) returns attention with the blocker "Auto land off after <kind> bounce", the bounce in issues[], and a repair of kind auto_land_off: fix the cause, then turn Auto land back on or enqueue. auto_land_switched_off (returned only when the PR has no live blocker of its own): Auto land was switched off without a bounce (queue entry cancelled, or nothing left to land); do not patch, push or turn it back on yourself, tell the human. A Vortex request_changes handoff at the live head returns attention with blocker "Vortex findings need a person" and repair kind vortex_findings; verify its findings against the live head. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: stack_wait
tools.description: Wait for a stack to need attention. Returns a mergestorm.stack_watch/v1 envelope; timeout_s: 0 returns one snapshot and timeout_s: 1-45 waits up to that many seconds, returning the current status (waiting or in_progress) if a snapshot was read and no attention is found. A timeout with either of those statuses is not a failure; waiting and in_progress end this slice, and the next call is stack_wait again with the same cursor. A timeout of failed means no assessment was produced. A stack that no longer exists returns status failed with watch.done true (reason not_found) and is not an error. While Cyclone or Vortex is still working on the blocked PR it returns in_progress, not attention, with busy[] naming the PR, blocker, and agent; agents carries that PR's vortexStatus, cycloneStatus, vortexReview, and busy flags. A blocker no agent run clears (a merge conflict vs the live parent, a restack Conflict or Restack failed, a Draft PR, a seam review pending with no review running, "Seam review stuck in reviewing, no review running", "Seam re-review pending, no review running", "Seam verdict is for an older head, no review running", or a review skipped for review quota) is still named during that in_progress, in blocker, prNumber, headSha, and issues[], with actAfter: "agents_idle" and waitingOn listing the busy agents: plan the fix, and act when a snapshot after the agents finish returns attention, re-reading the blocker then. Blockers the agents can change keep blocker and actAfter null. Attention never calls for changing a PR's GitHub base. When present, repair names the concrete fix for attention (restack_conflict and merge_conflict carry liveParent, never mg-park-*). For the three stuck-seam blockers, repair kind seam_review_stuck: do not patch or push; tell the human to click Continue, which re-queues the seam review at the live head. A pending land gate (landGatePending) returns in_progress, not attention. Auto land off after a merge_failed, gh_error, or ci_timeout bounce (the stack's autoLandOff reads reason bounced) returns attention with the blocker "Auto land off after <kind> bounce", the bounce in issues[], and a repair of kind auto_land_off: fix the cause, then turn Auto land back on or enqueue. auto_land_switched_off (returned only when the PR has no live blocker of its own): Auto land was switched off without a bounce (queue entry cancelled, or nothing left to land); do not patch, push or turn it back on yourself, tell the human. A Vortex request_changes handoff at the live head returns attention with blocker "Vortex findings need a person" and repair kind vortex_findings; verify its findings against the live head. Follow watch.next.args until watch.done; background watching requires a confirmed host notification. See server instructions.

tools.name: queue_status
tools.description: List live merge queue entries (position >= 1) plus the newest bounced entries (position 0) with bounceDetail for the current user, optionally filtered by stack.

tools.name: repo_settings_get
tools.description: Read the repository-level Auto patch, Auto review and Auto land values for the repositories connected to this account. Each value is true, false, or null; null means not set, so the account setting applies. Auto patch and Auto review precedence is the stack override (stack_set), then the repository value, then the account setting (settings_get). The Auto land repository value only seeds new stacks at adoption; it does not override an existing stack. Pass repo as owner/repo for one repository, or omit it for all.

tools.name: repo_settings_set
tools.description: Set Auto patch (Cyclone), Auto review (Vortex) or the Auto land default for every stack and pull request in one repository connected to this account, and return the stored result. true or false sets the repository value; null clears it so the account setting applies again. A stack override (stack_set) still wins for that stack. auto_patch and auto_review apply to open stacks without an override from their next decision; nothing is cancelled or re-queued. auto_land only seeds new stacks. Only the account that connected the repository can change it. Never changes account settings.

tools.name: settings_get
tools.description: Read the Bearer /api/v1/settings toggles, including auto_patch_enabled, auto_land_settle_seconds (how long Auto land waits before queueing), merge_queue_batch_enabled and merge_queue_batch_size (whether the merge queue tests several pull requests on one CI run, and how many), cyclone_connected (the Cyclone auto-patch App), and stacks_ready (whether stacks, the merge queue and Auto land can run for this account, which needs Mergestorm Surge).

tools.name: settings_set
tools.description: Update writable Bearer /api/v1/settings values and return the stored result. At least one key is required. auto_land_settle_seconds is a whole number of seconds from 15 through 300; it applies to settle clocks that start after the write. merge_queue_batch_enabled turns merge queue batching on or off for the account, and merge_queue_batch_size is a whole number from 2 through 8. cyclone_connected and github_connected are read-only and cannot be set.

instructions:
When stack work is done:
- Stack work is done only when the stack is landed, or when the human takes it back (archives it or tells you to stop). A clean push, a submit, an adopt, or one merged layer is not done: merging a lower layer can break a layer above it.
- Every stack_wait, stack_status, stack_adopt, and stack_set result carries watch: {done, until, reason, next, message}. While watch.done is false, keep calling stack_wait with watch.next.args (the returned cursor), 45s at a time, or hand the waiting to the background watcher below, and do not end your task. Stop only when watch.done is true.
- Only when your host has a confirmed notification that resumes this task, run `mg stack watch <stack-id>` as a background command with a notification on output matching `MS-WATCH (ATTENTION|LANDED)`, then end your turn. The watcher runs stack_wait against the Mergestorm API in slices of at most 300s, carries the cursor, stays silent while the stack is waiting or in_progress (busy[] holds and actAfter included), and costs no model tokens. It exits on attention (`MS-WATCH ATTENTION pr=<n> head=<sha> blocker=... repair=<kind>`, exit 3), on reads that keep failing (`MS-WATCH ATTENTION failed`, exit 3, after an auth or other permanent error twice, or after 15 minutes of timeouts and 5xx; tell the human the stack is no longer watched), on a closed, archived, or missing stack (`MS-WATCH ATTENTION stack=<id> reason=<reason>`, exit 3; verify missing stacks before reporting a landing), or on a confirmed landing (`MS-WATCH LANDED stack=<id> reason=landed`, exit 0). On an attention wake, read stack_status once, fix the blocker per mergestorm-bounce-watch, push, and start `mg stack watch <stack-id> --head <pushed-sha>` again. The command monitors the stack; it cannot wake an agent by itself. A confirmed notification is a host feature you can name that turns the command's exit or matching output into your next turn; a process left running, or output written to a log or terminal you do not read, is not one. Without a confirmed notification, keep using stack_wait with watch.next.args, or report that automatic follow-up is unavailable before ending the turn. Ending your turn while the watcher runs is not ending the task. Do not subscribe to GitHub events to wait on a stack.
- A layer PR shown as merged is merged into mg-stack-<n>, not main. The stack is landed only when the land PR (head mg-stack-<n>) merges into main or watch.done says landed. Never judge landing from GitHub PR state alone.
- attention means something for you to fix; repair, when present, names the concrete fix. A pending land gate (landGatePending: ci_pending) is a wait, not attention.

When you handle Vortex findings from review_wait_pr:
- Verify each finding against the current checkout. Do not treat the finding text as proven.
- Prefer the smallest correct patch. Do not refactor around a finding.
- Patch concrete bugs. A chat-only explanation is not a dismiss.
- A finding a human must decide (Decision required, policy fork, needs a human) stays open. Do not dismiss it and do not post the dismiss marker for it: tell the human which finding it is and stop.
- A PR comment whose first line is mergestorm-loop: dismiss is not a note about one finding. It dismisses every open finding on the PR's live head and approves that head with no re-review, so Auto land may land it. Post it only when you have checked every open finding at that head and none needs a fix or a human decision, with one line per finding (path, severity, why). Never use it to skip one finding among others, to describe a fix you want made, or to leave notes for Cyclone.
- Do not prefix that comment with cyclone-outcome: (reserved).
- A single finding you verified is wrong or not reproducible is dismissed by id with review_dismiss (or mg dismiss): pass the PR's live head_sha, the review_id, the finding_ids (preview: true lists them) and a reason. That is the only agent path that clears a seam gate, and only once every finding of that seam review is dismissed. Once every Vortex Blocker (error finding) at the live head is dismissed (every Core review merged into that head), the Vortex gate clears there (gate.vortex.cleared); otherwise gate.vortex.message says what still holds it. The dismiss comment alone resumes the review but does not clear the seam gate.
- Never dismiss a finding you did not check, one a human must decide, or findings of a newer review.

Stack PR bases (Mergestorm sets these; leave them):
- Stack of 2+ PRs: after adopt (stack_adopt, mg stack adopt, or mg stack submit) the bottom PR's GitHub base is the owned trunk mg-stack-<n>, not main. That is correct. Layer 2 is based on layer 1; layer 3+ on the mg-park-* freeze; the git parent of layer 2+ is still the layer below. A 1-PR stack stays on main and gets no mg-stack-<n>.
- Never retarget a stack PR's GitHub base (gh pr edit --base, a REST base change, or the UI). Moving the bottom to main makes Mergestorm abandon the stack's review unit; setting mg-stack-<n> again does not restore it. If a base was already moved, stop and tell the human; do not run stack land or re-adopt to repair it.
- mg-stack-<n> is the bottom PR's live parent: merging it into the bottom branch is that PR's conflict repair (bounce-watch rules). Never push to mg-stack-<n> except as the land PR's own repair: once every layer is promoted, the land PR's head is mg-stack-<n> and its live parent is its base (main), so merging main into mg-stack-<n>, or a CI fix on it, with an ordinary push (no force) is that repair. Fix the land PR only when busy[] shows no Cyclone run on it. Never rebase or merge layer 2+ onto mg-stack-<n> or onto main. mg-park-* is never a merge or rebase target.
- mg stack submit prints the base each PR opened with; the bottom moves to mg-stack-<n> right after. stack_status trunkBranch is the current trunk.

Stack-watch facts (mergestorm.stack_watch/v1):
- waiting with nonempty issues[] is not idle; in_progress can also carry issues[].
- assessment unavailable does not mean issue-free. timeout_s: 0 reads one enrich and one queue snapshot.
- Restack clean does not mean mergeable or CI-green.
- attention names the blocked PR via prNumber/headSha; currentCandidate is the promote candidate. Attention is not a mutation or authorization to change policy.
- verifyHeadSha is a queue verification SHA, not the live PR head.
- Do not patch a bounced PR while Cyclone or Vortex is still working on it. stack_wait and stack_status enforce this: they return in_progress instead of attention, with busy[] naming the PR, blocker, and agent, and agents carrying that PR's vortexStatus, cycloneStatus, vortexReview, and busy flags. in_progress with a nonempty busy[] means wait. Recheck the live remote PR head right before pushing.
- seam_pending alone, and a queued Vortex run older than 15 minutes, do not hold. A queued Vortex run holds for at most 15 minutes; reviewing and patching hold until the run finishes or its lease or check run is cleared; if it looks stuck, refresh stack_status and tell the human.
- A blocker no Vortex or Cyclone run clears (a merge conflict vs the live parent, a restack Conflict or Restack failed, a Draft PR, a seam review pending with no review running, "Seam review stuck in reviewing, no review running", "Seam re-review pending, no review running", "Seam verdict is for an older head, no review running", or a review skipped for review quota) stays in_progress during the hold but is named in blocker, prNumber, headSha, and issues[], with actAfter: "agents_idle" and waitingOn listing the busy agents. Plan the fix; act only when a snapshot after the agents finish returns attention, and re-read the blocker then. Blockers the agents can change keep blocker null and appear only in busy[]. For the three stuck-seam blockers, repair kind seam_review_stuck: do not patch or push; tell the human to click Continue, which re-queues the seam review at the live head.
- stack.autoEnqueueSettle with action ready or promote means Auto land found Cyclone and Vortex idle on that PR's green head and started its settle clock. action mergeability is published earlier, on a head that may not be green or idle yet.
- mg-park-* is a frozen GitHub base, not a repair target: never merge or rebase onto mg-park-*.
- merge_failed, gh_error, and ci_timeout bounces turn Auto land off, and stack autoLandOff then reads reason bounced with that queue entry's id; any other autoLandOff reason (user, archive, watcher, cancelled, landed) is not a bounce to undo. The watching agent turns Auto land back on with stack_set auto_land: true once it has handled that bounce, at most once per bounce and 3 times per watch; mergestorm-bounce-watch has the conditions.
- A stack whose layers are all merged into mg-stack-N but which has no open land PR (the branch was deleted, or the land PR cannot be opened) returns attention: blocker "No open land PR for mg-stack-N ...", repair kind land_pr_unavailable. Do not patch or push; tell the human to restore the branch from the closed land PR's head or close the stack.
- While stack autoLandOff reads reason bounced, the watch returns attention: blocker "Auto land off after <kind> bounce", the bounce in issues[], repair kind auto_land_off.
- While stack autoLandOff reads reason cancelled or watcher and the current PR has no live blocker of its own (a live blocker is reported first, with its own repair), the watch returns attention: blocker "Auto land switched off: <why>", repair kind auto_land_switched_off. No bounce did it and the layers need no change: do not patch, push or turn Auto land back on yourself; tell the human, who decides whether to turn it back on.
- A stack whose review unit was abandoned (a human moved its bottom PR off mg-stack-N) returns attention: blocker "Review unit abandoned: based on <base>", repair kind unit_abandoned. Do not patch or retarget; ask the human whether to re-root it. If at least two PRs remain open, tell them that mg stack adopt owner/repo#<bottom PR> re-roots it on a new review unit. With only one open PR, re-adopting will not create a review unit, so tell them to close and resubmit it to create a fresh stack.
- Auto land records why it is waiting (stack autoLandWait: reason, prNumber, headSha, since). The watch returns attention on that PR when the wait cannot clear on its own: a failing check Auto land reads live on GitHub, even while the ledger shows CI green (blocker "CI failed — Auto land reads a failing check on GitHub at this head", repair kind ci_failure); a check pending for 45 minutes (repair kind ci_pending); no approving Vortex review for 30 minutes with no Vortex run working (repair kind vortex_not_green); and a promote GitHub refused 3 times with merge_failed, after which Auto land stops retrying that head (repair kind promote_failed). It also returns attention when GitHub refuses to let Mergestorm read the head's check runs or commit statuses (blocker "Mergestorm cannot read ... on this head", repair kind ci_unreadable: do not patch or push; tell the human to grant the Mergestorm GitHub App the permission the repair names), and when any other wait reason has held for 45 minutes, a land gate left pending or running on the land PR included (blocker "Auto land has waited <N>m: <reason in plain words>", repair kind auto_land_waiting: read stack_status, fix what a commit on the named branch can fix, otherwise tell the human what Auto land waits for and since when). A more specific blocker on that PR is named first. A new head clears the wait.
- While the stack has a live merge queue entry, stack_wait carries queueWait (the entry's wait reason, how long it has been held, and the stack queued ahead of it) and the status line names it. The watch returns attention, blocker "Merge queue stuck: ..." and repair kind queue_stalled, when the entry (or the entry ahead of it) has been held for 45 minutes without landing or bouncing, or has sat queued for 45 minutes with nothing working on it or ahead of it.
- When no Vortex run works on the head and its review was skipped because auto-review is off (blocker "Vortex auto-review is off, so this head was not reviewed") or because billing could not be confirmed ("Vortex skipped this head: it could not confirm billing"), or it covered only part of the PR ("Vortex reviewed only part of this PR"), the watch returns attention at once with repair kind vortex_skipped. Do not patch for it; the repair names the mention or setting that gets the head reviewed.
- A live-head Vortex request_changes handoff returns attention with blocker "Vortex findings need a person" and repair kind vortex_findings; verify the review and inline findings against the live head before repair.
- Cyclone, with auto-patch on, patches only Vortex review findings (Core and seam, on any layer, the land PR included). It does not fix merge conflicts, restack conflicts, failing CI, or any other landing blocker by itself; the watching agent fixes those, whatever the auto-patch setting, and does not turn auto-patch off to do it. With auto-resolve conflicts on for the stack, Cyclone resolves a layer conflict itself (never the land PR's conflict with main): while busy[] shows Cyclone, wait, and fix the conflict only after its handoff, when the watch returns attention. With auto-fix CI on for the stack, Cyclone fixes a settled red check on a layer itself (never the land PR), or asks Surge for one re-run of a flaky one: while busy[] shows Cyclone, wait, and fix the failure only after its handoff, when the watch returns attention.
- Cyclone patches Vortex findings on a land PR when auto-patch is on for that stack (its override, else the account setting); every other land PR blocker, a conflict with main or failing CI included, is fixed by the watching agent on mg-stack-<n>.
- More states the watch names: a Vortex review skipped because the PR author is on the ignored authors list or because reviews are turned off for the repository is attention at once with repair kind vortex_skipped; a Vortex retry that is scheduled ("Vortex hit a temporary error on this head and will retry by itself") is a wait listed in issues[], never attention; "Review failed" carries repair kind vortex_failed (comment @mergestorm-vortex review or push a new commit; if it fails again tell the human); a PR open on mg-stack-N that is not a layer of the stack is attention at once, blocker "The land PR cannot be queued: ...", repair kind members_remaining (do not patch or push; close, retarget or adopt that PR).
- Use the mergestorm-bounce-watch skill for the fix-then-watch policy.
